headline: 7-0 win: Bangladesh women thrash Chinese Taipei in Junior Asia Cup opener
summary: The junior women's hockey team made a dominant start to their campaign in China, scoring seven goals in the final three quarters.
details: Bangladesh secured a stunning 7-0 victory over Chinese Taipei in their opening match of the Junior Asia Cup on Saturday in China.
After a goalless first quarter, the Bangladeshi side took complete control, scoring seven goals across the remaining three periods of the match.
Kona Akter broke the deadlock in the 20th minute, followed by two goals each from Nadira Ema and Irene Akter in the third quarter.
Sarika Rimon capped off the dominant performance with two penalty-corner goals in the final quarter, scoring in the 51st and 57th minutes.
The team, making only their second appearance in the tournament, previously finished ninth in the 2024 edition.
Bangladesh will now face Pakistan in their next Challenger Pool match tomorrow.
caption:
A dominant 7-0 victory! 🇧🇩
Bangladesh women's junior hockey team starts their Asia Cup campaign with a massive win.

Bangladesh secured a stunning 7-0 victory over Chinese Taipei in their opening match of the Junior Asia Cup on Saturday in China.

After a goalless first quarter, the Bangladeshi side took complete control, scoring seven goals across the remaining three periods of the match.

Kona Akter broke the deadlock in the 20th minute, followed by two goals each from Nadira Ema and Irene Akter in the third quarter.

Sarika Rimon capped off the dominant performance with two penalty-corner goals in the final quarter, scoring in the 51st and 57th minutes.

The team, making only their second appearance in the tournament, previously finished ninth in the 2024 edition.

Bangladesh will now face Pakistan in their next Challenger Pool match tomorrow.

Source: The Daily Star, Jamuna TV

headline_marked: No [[PM visit to India before UNGA session]], says State Minister
headline: No PM visit to India before UNGA session, says State Minister
summary: State Minister for Foreign Affairs Humaiun Kobir confirms no immediate trip to India, while the PM is set to carry a 'New Bangladesh' message to the UN.
details: State Minister for Foreign Affairs Humaiun Kobir announced that there is no possibility of a prime ministerial visit to India before the United Nations General Assembly (UNGA) session.
While bilateral discussions regarding a schedule are ongoing, the Minister emphasized that relations between India and Bangladesh must be based on mutual respect, engagement, and national interest.
The Prime Minister is expected to travel to the UN with a message focusing on the progress of 'New Bangladesh,' with a potential meeting with US President Donald Trump during the trip.

Addressing other diplomatic ties, Kobir noted that Bangladesh maintains strong relationships with the US, China, Saudi Arabia, and Middle Eastern countries, and is developing an effective working relationship with Russia.

Regarding the purchase of Boeing aircraft from the US, the Minister clarified that the decision was based on national need rather than external pressure, stating that Boeing or Airbus would be bought as required.
He also mentioned that discussions are underway regarding the Mecca agreement, noting that joining such an agreement would not be unusual for Bangladesh as it acts in its own national interest.
caption:
No Prime Ministerial visit to India before the UNGA session. State Minister Humaiun Kobir outlines the 'New Bangladesh' message for the world.

State Minister for Foreign Affairs Humaiun Kobir announced that there is no possibility of a prime ministerial visit to India before the United Nations General Assembly (UNGA) session.

While bilateral discussions regarding a schedule are ongoing, the Minister emphasized that relations between India and Bangladesh must be based on mutual respect, engagement, and national interest.

The Prime Minister is expected to travel to the UN with a message focusing on the progress of 'New Bangladesh,' with a potential meeting with US President Donald Trump during the trip.

Addressing other diplomatic ties, Kobir noted that Bangladesh maintains strong relationships with the US, China, Saudi Arabia, and Middle Eastern countries, and is developing an effective working relationship with Russia.

Regarding the purchase of Boeing aircraft from the US, the Minister clarified that the decision was based on national need rather than external pressure, stating that Boeing or Airbus would be bought as required.

He also mentioned that discussions are underway regarding the Mecca agreement, noting that joining such an agreement would not be unusual for Bangladesh as it acts in its own national interest.

Source: Dhaka Tribune, The Daily Star, Jamuna TV
